transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. What brings you here today?

I... I guess I came because I can’t stop feeling like I’m a danger to people. Like that near-miss means I’m not supposed to be a nurse, and... I’m just a disappointment. Sometimes it feels like everyone would be better off without me.
Have you had any thoughts about hurting yourself or ending your life?
I... I don’t have a plan or anything. It’s more like... sometimes I think it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up. Or if I could disappear, so I don’t mess anything up again.
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, or that you’ve lost interest in activities you once liked?

Yeah… I guess so. I used to do stuff to clear my head—jogging, knitting, cooking, reading after class. Now I mostly just… sit on my bed in my scrubs and I can’t really make myself care about any of it.
Have you been feeling this way most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

Yeah… it’s been most days. For a long time, actually. I think it started after I finished high school and started college classes and working full-time at the clinic… so, about a year and a couple months.
Have you been blaming yourself for things more than usual, or feeling like you’re a bad person or worthless?

Yeah… I do. A lot.

I keep thinking that… that near-miss means I’m not supposed to be a nurse. Like I’m dangerous, or just a disappointment. And it’s hard not to feel like everyone would be better off if I wasn’t around messing things up.
Have there been times when you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or extremely confident—like you didn’t need much sleep or that you could take on more than usual?
No… I don’t think so. I haven’t really had times like that. Not that I can remember.
Have you had days when you felt so down or depressed that it was hard to get through the day, and if so, how often has that happened?

Yeah… most days. I usually wake up with this heavy, empty feeling in my chest, and then I just… try to get through it. Even at the clinic, smiling and talking to patients, I feel like I’m barely keeping it together.
Have you noticed that your movements have slowed down, or that you can't sit still — like you're moving in slow motion or, on the flip side, that you're extra restless?

A little, yeah. People at the clinic have asked if I’m tired… I guess because I’m moving slower, like getting supplies takes me longer. Sometimes even simple questions take me a few seconds to answer.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently, like not feeling hungry or losing weight without trying?

Yeah… I guess so. I don’t really feel hungry much. I’ll forget to eat until pretty late, and then maybe just have crackers or coffee. My work pants have been looser too… I’m not trying to lose weight or anything.
Have you noticed that your depression has made it hard for you to do your job well or to keep up with your responsibilities at work?

Yeah… it has. I’ve fallen behind in my nursing prerequisites, and at work I don’t feel as sure of myself. I’ve had coworkers double-check things I used to just handle on my own, so now I get nervous taking on normal clinic stuff.
Before this current period of feeling down, have you had other times in your life when you felt this way for several weeks or more?
I don’t really know. Not like this, I don’t think… maybe I’ve had bad weeks before, but I can’t remember it lasting like this.
Before this current period of feeling down, have you ever had a time when you felt this level of depression for more than just a few days?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I’ve had rough patches, but I don’t remember it being this bad or lasting like this before.
Have you ever had a previous episode of depression that lasted for several weeks or more, before this current period?
I don’t know… I don’t think so. I’ve had times where I felt low, but I can’t really say it lasted for weeks like this.
